notes:
Account summary: mid-market product analytics company focused on in-app guidance and queryable product documentation. Started on Redwood hosted API for embeddings + chat in Q3 2025; impressed with latency, moved to an eval POC for Dedicated in Jan 2026.

POC highlights (short):
- POC config: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (shared dev pool) for 3-week trial; sequence lengths avg 512 tokens for assistant flows, 2048 for nightly batch rerank.
- Performance: 90th p95 token latency 22ms for convo path, peak throughput 120 requests/sec with batching. Observability dashboard valued by infra team.
- Quality: model -> redwood-curated-1 (quantized) meets internal quality bar for answers, minor regressions on long-context summarization flagged.

Pricing/packaging negotiation context:
- Primary ask from Verdance: fixed committed capacity (monthly GPU hours) with clear burst and overage rules; want predictable unit economics as they move from pilot to paid tier.
- They prefer 12-24 month committed contract with stepped ramp: 25% commit month1, 50% month4, 100% month10 (proposal from finance). Want ability to burst 2x baseline for short windows without punitive overage.
- Key commercial asks: lower committed rate if they accept annual pre-pay; optional burst pool priced at blended GPU-hour + per-token surcharge for very high seq lengths. Finance requested examples of billing scenarios (50%, 75%, 125% usage) to show monthly cashflow.
- Technical asks tied to pricing: ability to pin model versions per route, soft-fallback to cheaper model family automatically when reserved pool saturated, and transparent token-level cost breakdowns in Console for chargeback.

Security/compliance discussion:
- Must have VPC peering and SSO/SAML. SOC2 report needed prior to final signature. KMS integration required for encryption at rest. Retention controls: 90-day ephemeral KV cache for PII and 7-year audit log retention for product events (legal ask).

Negotiation status and redlines:
- Legal flagged two clauses: data residency (want EU residency option for EU customers), and indemnity cap — Redwood proposed standard; Verdance requested carveouts for third-party data.
- Pricing redline: Verdance pushing for a 20% discount on list committed rate at $200k ARR threshold, and a 10% credit against overage if they cross monthly commit by less than 20%.
- SE note: requested formal pricing scenarios + sample invoice for first 6 months. Asking for a SOW that explicitly lists ramp schedule and a defined burst grace of 48 hours per incident.

Quotes/voice of customer (short):
- "We need predictable cost as feature usage scales—surprises kill the roadmap." — Head of Product (Lena Morris).
- "Observability and token-level chargeback are a must for us to get internal wdgs (workload owners) to adopt." — Infrastructure Lead (Jamal Rivera).
